title: Schedule optimization for tau-leaping in masked discrete diffusion
summary: Masked diffusions are popular generative models for discrete distributions. Unlike standard autoregressive sampling, they reveal several coordinates in parallel, approximating each block's joint conditional law by a product of one-coordinate conditionals. The resulting procedure, usually called tau-leaping, reduces computational cost but introduces a factorization error ($\varepsilon_\text{fact}$), even with perfectly learned predictors.
